record.original_question: For a projective billiard, when does the system possess an invariant symplectic form, and when does it admit a variational description?

evidence.quote: Serge Tabachnikov Projective billiards.Projective billiards were defined in [107]. A projective billiard table is a convex domain with smooth boundary equipped with a transverse field of directions; the phase space is the same as that of the conventional billiard, and the reflection law is such that the tangential component of the incoming velocity vector is preserved, whereas the transverse component is reversed. Problem:when does a projective billiard possess an invariant symplectic form?And, related, when does it have a variational description?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $
u$ be a smooth field of directions along $\partial\Omega$ that is everywhere transverse to $\partial\Omega$ (a "projective billiard structure"). Define the projective billiard map on the phase space of oriented lines meeting $\partial\Omega$ (equivalently, unit tangent vectors based at $\partial\Omega$ pointing inward) by the following reflection rule at each impact point $p \in \partial\Omega$: decompose the incoming velocity vector into a component tangent to $\partial\Omega$ at $p$ and a component along the transverse direction $
u(p)$; the tangential component is preserved while the transverse (along $
u(p)$) component is reversed. The resulting outgoing direction together with the next impact point on $\partial\Omega$ defines the next state.

(a) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(\partial\Omega,
u)$ under which the projective billiard map admits an invariant symplectic form on its phase space.

(b) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $(\partial\Omega,
u)$ under which the projective billiard map admits a variational (least-action) description, i.e., its orbits arise as critical points of a generating functional analogous to the length functional in the standard billiard.

status_evidence.title: On Hamiltonian projective billiards on boundaries of convex bodies
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work classifies special cases of projective billiards admitting Hamiltonian/symplectic structure.
status_evidence.claim: Only special/partial cases are known; general characterization is not established.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in recent compilations of open problems in billiards. Partial results are known (e.g., projective billiards on a sphere with an exactness condition on the transverse field admit an invariant symplectic form induced by the hyperbolic Beltrami-Cayley-Klein metric, and recent work studies Hamiltonian projective billiards on convex bodies), but a complete characterization of when an invariant symplectic form or a variational description exists remains open.
